title: Lesson 22. async/await and error handling
description: async, await, try/catch and a loading indicator

learn.intro: Hi! Lesson 22 — **async/await**. A .then().then() chain is hard to read. We'll learn to write asynchronous code line by line like normal code. Let's go!

slides.text: Both do the same thing, but the second reads **top to bottom**.

check.prompt: async/await and .then do the same thing but are written differently.
check.explain: The second reads like normal code.

slides.text:
`async` before a function — «this function can wait».
`await` before a call — «stop on this line until the result arrives».

options: Waits for the result on this line
check.explain: await pauses until the result comes.

check.prompt: What goes before a function so it can use await?

slides.text: `try` — we try to run it, `catch` — what to do on an error: the internet is gone or the server is down.
To test it: in DevTools open the **Network** tab and turn on **Offline**. The request fails and `catch` runs.

check.prompt: When does the catch block run?
options: When an error happened in try

slides.text: While waiting for data we show «Loading…», on an error a message:
Practice: rewrite the fetch from the last lesson with `async/await` and `try/catch`. Homework: add a «Loading…» indicator and an error message to your API project.

check.prompt: When should the «Loading...» label be cleared?
check.explain: The data came — the indicator is no longer needed.

questions.prompt: Which version reads top to bottom?
questions.explain: async/await is written like normal code.

questions.prompt: async before a function means «this function can wait».
questions.explain: So you can use await inside.

questions.prompt: What does await before a call mean?

questions.explain: await works only in an async function.

questions.prompt: If everything went fine in try, the catch block runs too.
How do you check that catch works?
Which word catches the error after try? (one word)
What do we show the user on a request error?
options: A blank screen with no explanation
questions.explain: The user needs to understand what happened.

questions.prompt: Where do you put «Loading...» in an async function?
questions.explain: First show the indicator, then request the data.
